function: ISAC transmit design: LLM-generated candidate BS precoders, with user and target distance-angle variables, trading communication rate against sensing CRB in a multi-objective problem (p. 6, p. 8).
system: BS with N-antenna ULA, K single-antenna users/targets, near-field monostatic ISAC, no RIS (p. 3, p. 5); carrier unstated, 28 GHz merely illustrative (p. 4); 51.2 MHz bandwidth (p. 10).
method: Pretrained GPT-4.0 LLM as black-box reproduction operator inside a GWO-based decomposition MOEA, via prompting and in-context learning; no training or fine-tuning (p. 7, p. 9, p. 10).
data_channel: Synthetic single-path near-field spherical-wave channel with constant free-space path-loss gain, -60 dB at 1 m; no training data, simulation only (p. 4, p. 10).
test_conditions: No training stage; one simulation setting: RCS magnitude uniform in [0.8, 1], 51.2 MHz, noise -110 dBm, power 0-20 dBm; N, K, carrier not reported (p. 9, p. 10).
baselines: Non-learned: GWO, MOEA/D [41]; learned: LEDMA [40], earlier LLM-enabled ISAC multi-objective metaheuristic (p. 10); Pareto front compares GWO only (p. 11).
metrics: Average fitness (Tchebycheff aggregation) versus iterations, Pareto front of communication rate versus sensing log-CRB objective, and transmit beampattern toward targets at 30 and 60 degrees (p. 11).
complexity: Order O(M^2+T(MCf+MD+Mno+M|Phi|)) for Algorithm 1 over T iterations, LLM treated as black-box oracle; no runtime or LLM inference cost reported (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "the channel between user k and the n-th antenna element can be expressed as" (eq. 11), whose gain "represents the free-space path loss of user/target k"; custom analytic model, no standardized, ray-traced, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 9: "The LLM does not perform online training or parameter updates"; all results use one fixed simulation setting (p. 10), with no change of scenario, band, or number of users or antennas.
q3_support: p. 10: "existing LLM-enabled metaheuristic algorithm, named as LEDMA [40], GWO, MOEA/D [41]"; p. 11: "provides higher power at the target locations than the LEDMA and" GWO-based methods (Fig. 7), and fitness "0.007, while the LEDMA and GWO achieve average fitness function value of 0.267 and 0.029".
q4_support: p. 10: "the overall computational complexity of Algorithm 1 over T iterations can be summarized as" O(M^2+T(MCf+MD+Mno+M|Phi|)).
q5_support: p. 10: "The magnitude of the RCS is assumed to be uniformly distributed in range in [0.8, 1]"; data are simulated from the analytic channel of p. 4; no code, data link, or public dataset anywhere in the paper.
notes: PDF matches the DOI (accepted manuscript, p. 1). Borderline on no_learning: the only learned component is a pretrained GPT-4.0 used through prompts and in-context learning, with no training or fine-tuning (p. 9, p. 10), as the reproduction operator that generates candidate solutions inside a GWO and decomposition metaheuristic (p. 7, p. 8). I counted it as learned because the LLM generates the candidate precoders; if the reviewer does not accept a prompted pretrained LLM as learned, the code is no_learning (p. 9). Area 5: the design trades communication rate against sensing CRB through BS precoding (p. 6); the decision variables also include the distances and angles of users and targets (p. 6). q3: LEDMA appears in the fitness (Fig. 5) and beampattern (Fig. 7) comparisons but not in the Pareto front (Fig. 6, GWO only), all on p. 11; please confirm that the final fitness value and the beampattern count as performance comparisons. q4: the complexity order treats the LLM as a black-box oracle (p. 10). The simulation setting omits N, K, and the carrier frequency (p. 10), and p. 11 mentions 'jailbreak prompts', an apparent copy error.
